title: Knowledge check: Cookies, Sessions, and Token Security

questions.prompt: In Cookies, Sessions, and Token Security, which statement best describes Secure cookie attributes?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Choose one coherent identity flow, verify credentials/tokens at the server, set expiration and revocation behavior, and configure cookies/tokens for the actual deployment threat model.
This option describes a different concept and does not define secure cookie attributes (choice 2).
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
questions.answer_key: Choose one coherent identity flow, verify credentials/tokens at the server, set expiration and revocation behavior, and configure cookies/tokens for the actual deployment threat model.
questions.explanation: Choose one coherent identity flow, verify credentials/tokens at the server, set expiration and revocation behavior, and configure cookies/tokens for the actual deployment threat model.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Cookies, Sessions, and Token Security?
options: Use secure configuration, HTTPS, narrow origin allowlists, secure cookies, rate and payload limits, parameterized database access, dependency updates, and context-aware output handling. One control never replaces authorization.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: Use secure configuration, HTTPS, narrow origin allowlists, secure cookies, rate and payload limits, parameterized database access, dependency updates, and context-aware output handling. One control never replaces authorization.
questions.explanation: Use secure configuration, HTTPS, narrow origin allowlists, secure cookies, rate and payload limits, parameterized database access, dependency updates, and context-aware output handling. One control never replaces authorization.

questions.prompt: A change related to Cookies, Sessions, and Token Security appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
